judgment.rationale: A commenter has already supplied a concrete fork-side implementation for the measured frame drift. The current upstream placement path still measures the frame once, so the commit is a candidate fix rather than a shipped resolution; no competing proposal is needed.
evidence: The original report describes a 5 px gap for custom-chrome applications in edge-touching FancyZones.
The 2026-10-25 comment measures Outlook's visible frame changing after FancyZones places it and reports a 3 px overshoot.
Current WorkArea::Snap calls AdjustRectForSizeWindowToRect and SizeWindowToRect once; current AdjustRectForSizeWindowToRect reads DWMWA_EXTENDED_FRAME_BOUNDS at placement time.
The contributor's fork commit 8330387cc9715c54dba0b3329c619c3a58296a74 adds a bounded frame recheck after placement.
The commit is on the contributor's fork and has not been merged upstream.
judgment.recommended_action: Review the contributor's existing fork commit and keep the issue open until the candidate is accepted, integrated, and verified.

fix_assessment.rationale: The issue thread links a concrete fork implementation that checks visible frame bounds for a bounded period after placement and corrects small drift. It is not an upstream or released fix.

issue_context.summary: FancyZones can leave gaps around custom-chrome windows after placement. A current comment measures the app changing its invisible resize border after placement, and links a fork-side bounded recheck patch.
known_information: The original report covers FancyZones 0.68.1 and describes a 5 px gap around windows such as Visual Studio or Unity in zones touching screen edges.
A 2024 comment reports that calling SetWindowPlacement later removes the gap.
The 2026-10-25 comment measures Outlook changing its invisible resize border about two seconds after placement; the visible frame then extends roughly 3 px beyond the zone.
Current WorkArea::Snap uses AdjustRectForSizeWindowToRect to measure the visible frame and then calls SizeWindowToRect once.
Current AdjustRectForSizeWindowToRect reads DWMWA_EXTENDED_FRAME_BOUNDS at that moment; the current path has no later frame reconciliation.
Commit 8330387cc9715c54dba0b3329c619c3a58296a74 on the contributor's fork adds bounded post-placement checks and correction attempts.
inferences: When an application changes its non-client border after FancyZones measures it, the window rectangle can stay constant while its visible frame drifts outside the zone.
The linked fork patch is a plausible correction, but its integration and long-term behavior have not been verified on upstream main.
issue_context.analysis: The new measurements make the timing boundary more precise than the earlier startup-delay hypothesis: the application changes its frame after placement. The contributor has already implemented a bounded recheck on a fork. Review that candidate rather than creating a competing fix; keep the issue open until it is integrated and verified.
